title: Cross-functional ad-hoc heatmap — owners & quick econ scan (Mar 2026)
body:
Purpose:
This is an ad-hoc, shareable single-sheet sketch to surface immediate coverage gaps and a light economic (hours + estimated cost) signal across a handful of cross-functional owners for the next 6 weeks. Not a canonical plan — quick triage artifact intended for sync or async review by leads.

Context / why now:
- Prep for sprint boundary + planned canary on 2026-03-25 where we expect increased routing churn and a potential fallback ramp.
- We need a compact owner map and a rough hourly/cost view to decide whether to staff a short-term surge or rely on existing on-call commitments.

Scope (what this sheet covers):
- Runtime routes and fallback coverage for high-traffic tenants (top 10 by qps).
- Short-lived special projects (model swap tests, quantization pilot) that may consume Dedicated pool capacity.
- Observability & playbook readiness for the new canary (tracing hooks + runbooks).

How to read the heatmap (quick):
- Rows = functional ownership buckets (runtime, infra, monitoring, product, SE/customer-impact).
- Columns = risk buckets for the next 6 weeks: Routine, Elevated, Canary-week, Peak-week, Post-canary-smoke.
- Cell color (textual here): GREEN = covered within current oncall/shift; YELLOW = stretch (can cover with re-prioritization, ~10-20% extra hours); RED = requires explicit surge hire/rotation (40%+ effort).

Compact heatmap (text grid):
- Runtime: Routine=GREEN, Elevated=YELLOW, Canary-week=RED, Peak-week=RED, Post-canary-smoke=YELLOW
- Infra: Routine=GREEN, Elevated=YELLOW, Canary-week=YELLOW, Peak-week=RED, Post-canary-smoke=YELLOW
- Observability: Routine=YELLOW, Elevated=YELLOW, Canary-week=RED, Peak-week=RED, Post-canary-smoke=YELLOW
- Product (routes/feature owners): Routine=GREEN, Elevated=YELLOW, Canary-week=YELLOW, Peak-week=YELLOW, Post-canary-smoke=GREEN
- SE / CS contact: Routine=GREEN, Elevated=GREEN, Canary-week=YELLOW, Peak-week=RED, Post-canary-smoke=GREEN

Owner table + quick hours estimate (6-week window):
- Runtime (owner: Alex Rivera) — baseline: 20h/wk; Canary-week incremental: +28h (on-call overlap + handoffs). Quick-est cost: 48h * $85/hr equiv = $4,080 (assume blended eng rate).
- Infra (owner: Marcus Li) — baseline: 8h/wk; Canary-week incremental: +24h. Quick-est cost: 32h * $90/hr = $2,880.
- Observability (owner: Jordan Kim) — baseline: 10h/wk; Canary-week incremental: +32h (dashboards + alert tuning + runbook updates). Quick-est cost: 42h * $75/hr = $3,150.
- Product (owner: Priya Shah) — baseline: 6h/wk; Canary-week incremental: +12h (customer comms + triage). Quick-est cost: 18h * $95/hr = $1,710.
- SE / CS (owner: Lila Gomez) — baseline: 6h/wk; Canary-week incremental: +20h. Quick-est cost: 26h * $60/hr = $1,560.

Total quick-est (incremental for Canary-week only): approx $13,380.
Assumptions: blended hourly rates are ballpark, hours are estimates for planning only. We do not include infra cloud $$$ here (GPU minutes) — separate cost sheet if needed.

Priority actions (immediate, owner):
1) Confirm coverage for Canary-week (2026-03-25 to 2026-03-31) — owners: Alex, Marcus — due 2026-03-19.
2) Lock a minimal escalation chain + phone rota for Peak-week — owner: Priya — due 2026-03-20.
3) Light observability smoke tests (synthetic traces + alert sanity) — owner: Jordan — run by 2026-03-22.
4) SE/CS pre-brief and canned comms (top-10 tenant list + likely impact phrasing) — owner: Lila — draft by 2026-03-21.

Quick mitigation levers (fast, low friction):
- Move non-essential infra work to next sprint (saves ~12h/wk across infra).
- Increase prioritization for KV-prefix caching for top 3 tenants (runtime config roll) — reduces per-token load ~8–12% (soft).
- Short-lived on-call augmentation: 2 cross-team volunteers for Canary-week (4h/day each) rather than full replacement — cheaper and faster.

Open questions / decision points (need :yes/:no):
- Do we authorize paid overtime/contractor coverage for Canary-week? (yes/no) — impacts hiring vs rotation cost.
- Are we comfortable relying on fallback model variant for Peak-week? (yes/no) — product tradeoff vs quality.
- Require a dedicated runbook post-mitigation for future rollouts? (yes/no)

Notes / quick provenance:
- Top-10 tenant qps taken from GA telemetry (snapshot 2026-03-06).
- Cost rates are blended internal estimates; for external chargebacks we should map to finance rates (linked artifact: JIRA OPS-1427).

Next steps (short):
- Triage sync (15m) with listed owners tomorrow (2026-03-20 09:00 PT). Priya to run; Alex to present runtime plan.
- If decisions are affirmative for paid augmentation, Priya/Marcus to prepare a one-line PO request and send to finance.

Quick checklist (for doc update after sync):
- [ ] Record confirmed rota + names in the sheet (owner: Alex).
- [ ] Attach final cost approval or rejection (owner: Priya).
- [ ] Publish 1-paragraph comms for customers (owner: Lila).
- [ ] Create follow-up ticket for observability gaps (owner: Jordan).

Small log (changes):
- 2026-03-09 initial draft (Priya).
- 2026-03-12 added runtime quick-est and heatmap (Alex).
- 2026-03-16 updated observability delta after smoke-run (Jordan).
- 2026-03-19 minor edits and sync scheduling (Priya).

If you want this expanded into a small sheet with auto-sum cells and conditional formatting I can convert this into a spreadsheet version (two tabs: heatmap + cost calc) — ping me and I will spin it up and link it here.

-- Priya
